name: Cursor
summary: Cursor is an AI-assisted code editor for professional software development, combining IDE workflows with coding assistance and agent-style features.

product.one_liner: AI-assisted code editor for professional software development
product.description: Cursor provides a code editing environment with integrated AI assistance. Public product and docs surfaces describe capabilities including agent workflows, rules, MCP, skills, CLI, code completion, chat over a codebase, and multi-file edits inside the editor.

market.problem: Developers want faster coding and editing while keeping repository context inside their primary development environment

business_model.notes: Public pricing lists individual and business/team subscription plans. Plan pages describe feature and usage differences by tier.

ai_profile.model_strategy: Editor product orchestrates model-backed coding assistance, chat, and agent workflows; public materials emphasize product integration rather than owning a frontier base model
ai_profile.data_advantage: Potential advantage from IDE interaction loops and codebase context workflows; extent of proprietary data advantage is not fully public
ai_profile.notes: AI capability is structural: completion, chat, edits, and agents are core to the product. Without model-backed assistance, the offering collapses to a conventional editor fork.

traction.notes: No ARR, seat counts, or download metrics are included. community_signals and hiring_signals are omitted until sourced. Category popularity claims are omitted. product_led is not claimed: website signup/download exists, but PLG expansion mechanics are not evidenced beyond direct web access.

funding.notes: TechCrunch (2023-10-11) reported an OpenAI Startup Fund-led seed, but later rounds and totals are inconsistently reported elsewhere. Numeric fields remain null until a dated, complete funding snapshot is attached.

product.rationale: Judgment: coherent AI editor product with clear core workflows on the product site and matching developer docs.

market.rationale: Judgment: AI developer tools is a clear, active category with identifiable peers. Capped at 4: company site + one news article do not meet the category-evidence bar for 5.

business_model.rationale: Judgment: public subscription pricing provides a clear monetization path.

technology.rationale: Judgment (application layer): meaningful editor orchestration, context, and agent workflows versus peers; not frontier-model ownership. Calibrated against other AI developer tools, not model labs.

growth.rationale: Not scored: no sourced seats, revenue, or usage metrics in this entry.

competitive_position.rationale: Judgment (application layer): visible contender among AI coding products; defensibility versus Copilot/IDE incumbents and peer agents remains uncertain.

extensions.differentiation: Public positioning centers on an AI-first editor workflow rather than a plugin bolted onto a traditional IDE; durability of that differentiation versus peers is not measured here
extensions.confidence_notes: Product, docs, pricing, and founder identity are now primary-sourced. Funding totals, growth metrics, community intensity, and hiring remain weakly evidenced. product_led removed: self-serve signup exists, but PLG expansion mechanics are not evidenced beyond direct web access.
